name: CapCut Picture-In-Picture Border With Chroma Shape
use_when: A reaction, gaming, tutorial, or commentary layout needs a clean circular or shaped picture-in-picture frame.
CapCut's built-in mask gives the video shape but not the desired border styling.
A simple external shape matte can create the border faster than building a custom graphic in the NLE.
avoid_when: The border covers gameplay, UI, captions, product information, or proof.
The chroma-keyed border has jagged edges or green spill.
The PiP camera feed is too small to read the face or reaction.
The border style clashes with the project tone.

timeline_pattern.pattern: create_border_shape_on_key_color -> import_border_overlay -> chroma_key_key_color -> add_pip_video_overlay -> apply_matching_mask -> scale_inside_border -> position_safe -> qc_edges
timeline_pattern.shape_rule: Make the border shape cleaner and slightly larger than the PiP video mask.
timeline_pattern.key_rule: Use a key color that is absent from the border and video region, then tune intensity to remove only the background.
timeline_pattern.alignment_rule: Adjust PiP mask and scale after the border is in place so the border thickness is even.
timeline_pattern.safe_area_rule: Place PiP where it supports context without blocking UI, captions, or proof.

motion.rule: PiP and border should move together if animated; otherwise keep them stable so reactions remain readable.

keyframe_values.border_size: Create the border large enough to allow minor mask adjustment without exposing the keyed background.
keyframe_values.pip_scale: Scale the video slightly inside the border so the white/ring edge stays visible.
keyframe_values.corner_position: Use corners or planned negative space rather than the active action center.

sound.rule: PiP border graphics usually need no SFX; prioritize speaker/game/tutorial audio.

captions.rule: Keep captions away from the PiP region or move PiP above/beside the caption safe zone.

color.rule: Border color should contrast with the background while fitting the style; white is useful only when it remains visible on bright footage.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use an alpha border asset or key out a generated chroma background, overlay the PiP video clipped with an alpha/circle mask, and render edge-check frames.
implementation.remotion: Model PiP as video source, maskShape, borderAsset, borderColor, position, safeRegion, and chromaKey fields.
implementation.blender: Use a circular plane/alpha matte and border ring shape, then place the camera/video plane inside it.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Create a border shape on a green/key-colored background, import it as overlay, use Chroma Key to remove the key color, add the PiP video overlay, apply a matching Circle mask, scale it inside the border, and adjust position.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Essential Graphics shape layers or an alpha PNG border, crop/mask the PiP video, nest the pair, and keep the nested PiP caption-safe.

common_mistakes: Making the border and video mask different shapes so the edge looks uneven.
Leaving green spill or jagged chroma-key edges.
Placing PiP over gameplay UI, captions, or product proof.
Making the face too small to read.
Animating the border separately from the PiP video.
qc: Is the PiP face/reaction readable at delivery size?
Is the border edge clean with no key color spill?
Does the video mask align evenly inside the border?
Does the PiP avoid captions, UI, products, proof, and active action?
Do PiP and border stay synced if animated?
